cut: 3D v1 stills (19 Nov, en only). Owner, 19 Nov: 'Top3' then 'Go ahead with stills for A'. Device: the town's rulebook — a town clerk's typewriter types ordinance headings and each is stamped PREEMPTED (W. Va. Code §5B-2-21b, from HB 2014); the corkboard behind carries the recorded line and the two denials; the last sheet is the bill itself, ending DRAFTED BY: ____. v1.1 (19 Nov, owner: 'Check quotes and make the message clear'): captions rewritten to one plain line of story each; the stamp says EXEMPT; McGavran quoted from the Country Roads transcript, the version four outlets share. v2 (20 Nov, owner: 'The message was unclear… Is it against data centers?'): rebuilt in story order — the town's 5–0 no first and last, the law in plain words (stamp DOESN’T APPLY), the claim, the denials, and the stake: if certified, the town gets no say.
argument: West Virginia's law exempts state-certified data centers from towns' own noise, lighting and zoning rules; a Fundamental Data engineer said the company 'basically wrote the bill'; the company and the governor's office say it did not.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word

text.en: A town voted 5–0 / [against] / a data center.

captions.source: Town of Davis, W. Va.: council resolution opposing the planned data center, passed 5–0 (the card on the board, shown big). A resolution states the town's position; it is not a permit decision.

text.en: A state law says / the town’s rules / [don’t apply]. / Who wrote it?

captions.source: W. Va. Code §5B-2-21b(d)(1), from HB 2014 (2025; signed 30 Apr 2025): certified microgrid districts and certified high impact data centers 'may not be subject to' 'County or municipal zoning, horticultural, noise, viewshed, lighting, development, or land use ordinances, restrictions, limitations, or approvals'. Applies to state-certified projects only; uncertified data centers stay under local rules. Same wording in the 2026 enrolled HB 5168. Cross-checked 19 Nov across search results from several outlets; the primary page could not be opened from the build machine.

text.en: The developer’s / engineer: / “we were the guys / that basically / [wrote] the bill.”

captions.source: Ted McGavran, a Fundamental Data engineer, at the Belmont, N.C. City Council, 6 Jul 2026. Country Roads News transcript (21 Jul 2026): 'We were the guys that basically wrote the bill and got it through the legislature in 2024 and early '25.' The same core phrase in WV Watch (22 Jul; 'who' for 'that'), WVHC and the Parsons Advocate. Gray TV (13 Nov) prints a different version ('we're the guys that wrote the bill'); not used. Cross-checked 19 Nov across search results from several outlets; the primary page could not be opened from the build machine.

text.en: The developer and / the governor’s / office: [it didn’t].

captions.source: Fundamental Data (spokesperson Andrea Khoury): it 'did not draft, write or play any role in drafting HB 2014'; McGavran spoke for himself. Governor's office (spokesperson Lars Dalseide): HB 2014 was 'the Governor's bill', its drafting 'deliberately limited to the Governor's office' (WV Watch 22 Jul 2026; Country Roads; WVHC). Cross-checked 19 Nov across search results from several outlets; the primary page could not be opened from the build machine.

text.en: If it’s certified, / the town / gets [no say].

captions.source: W. Va. Code §5B-2-21b(d)(1): a certified high impact data center 'may not be subject to' municipal zoning, noise, lighting, development or land use ordinances or approvals. Conditional on purpose: no certification application filed yet (state data economy office; tag5).

props: No logos, no people, no faces. The typewriter, desk and corkboard are invented props. The ordinance is a generic blank (TOWN OF ____), not a Davis document. Quotes on the cards carry their speaker and outlet.

post.en: Davis, W. Va. voted 5–0 against a data center. A state law, HB 2014, says certified data centers don't follow towns' noise, lighting or zoning rules. A company engineer said "we were the guys that basically wrote the bill." The company and the governor's office say it didn't.
